title: Ema Datshi
instructions: Wash and slit the chilies lengthwise. Remove seeds if you prefer less heat.
In a pan, combine chilies, sliced onions, chopped tomatoes, garlic, vegetable oil, salt, and water.
Cover and bring to a boil over medium heat until the chilies are soft (about 8-10 minutes).
Add the sliced cheese on top and cover the pan without stirring for 2-3 minutes until the cheese melts.
Stir gently to incorporate the cheese into the broth. Serve hot with Bhutanese red rice.

title: Kewa Datshi
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes.
Place potatoes, sliced onions, chilies, garlic, butter, and salt in a pot with water.
Boil until the potatoes are tender and the water has reduced slightly.
Add the cheese and stir gently until it melts into a creamy sauce.
Garnish with spring onions and serve with red rice.

title: Shamu Datshi
instructions: Clean and slice the mushrooms.
In a pan, add mushrooms, butter, water, and sliced chilies.
Simmer until the mushrooms are tender and the water reduces.
Stir in the cheese and wait until it is fully melted and creamy.
Serve as a side dish or main over rice.

title: Phaksha Paa
instructions: Cut the pork into strips or cubes and sear in a pot until browned and the fat renders.
Add ginger, garlic, and onions, sautéing until fragrant.
Add dried red chilies and sliced radish.
Pour in stock or water and simmer for 30-40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in bok choy or spinach at the end and cook for another 5 minutes.

title: Jasha Maru
instructions: Heat oil and sauté garlic, ginger, and onions until soft.
Add the chicken (minced or diced) and brown evenly.
Stir in tomatoes, leeks, and chilies.
Add chicken stock and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Garnish with plenty of fresh coriander.

title: Zow Shungo
instructions: Sauté onions, garlic, and diced vegetables (potatoes, carrots) in oil until tender.
Add cabbage and cook until wilted.
Stir in leftover cooked rice and spices (turmeric, cumin, pepper).
Toss everything together until the rice is heated through and slightly crispy.
Optionally, melt some cheese into the mixture before serving.

title: Hoentay
instructions: Mix buckwheat flour with water to form a soft dough. Let it rest.
For the filling, sauté turnip leaves in butter until dry. Mix with cheese, ginger, garlic, and chili powder.
Roll out the dough into thin circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center, fold, and pleat to seal.
Steam the dumplings for 15-20 minutes until the wrapper is tender.

title: Suja
instructions: Boil water and add tea leaves. Simmer until the tea is dark brown.
Strain the tea to remove leaves.
Add butter and salt to the hot tea.
Churn the mixture using a traditional wooden churner (jasum) or a modern blender for 30 seconds until frothy.
Serve hot in small bowls.

title: Khuley
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour, salt and water into a smooth, thin batter.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and grease it lightly with butter.
Pour a ladle of batter and tilt the pan to spread it thin.
Cook for 2 minutes per side until the edges lift and brown spots appear.
Serve warm with Ezay or a little butter and cheese.

title: Tingmo
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in warm water and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix in the flour, salt and oil and knead into a smooth dough for 8 minutes.
Cover and let the dough rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into balls, roll out, brush with oil and roll up into spirals.
Steam for 15-20 minutes until fluffy and cooked through. Serve with Ema Datshi or Phaksha Paa.

title: Ezay
instructions: Finely chop the tomatoes, chilies, onion and coriander.
Crumble or grate the cheese.
Mix everything together with salt, squeezing lightly so the juices release.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve as a chili relish with rice, Khuley or Tingmo.

title: Beef Momo
instructions: Knead the flour, water and a pinch of salt into a firm dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef with finely chopped cabbage, onion, garlic, ginger, oil and salt for the filling.
Roll the dough into small circles, place a spoonful of filling in each and pleat to seal.
Steam in an oiled steamer for 12-15 minutes until the wrappers turn glossy.
Serve hot with Ezay on the side.

title: Puta
instructions: Knead the buckwheat flour with hot water into a stiff dough.
Press the dough through a noodle press into boiling water.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the noodles float, then drain.
Toss with butter, grated cheese, sliced spring onion, chili powder and salt.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Nakey Datshi
instructions: Wash the ferns well and cut them into short lengths.
Put the ferns, sliced onion, chilies, garlic, butter, salt and water in a pan.
Cook on medium heat for 8 minutes until the ferns are tender.
Add the cheese, cover and let it melt, then stir gently.
Serve with red rice.

title: Bhutanese Dal
instructions: Rinse the lentils and simmer them in water with turmeric for 20 minutes until soft.
Heat the oil and fry onion, garlic, ginger and chilies until golden.
Add the chopped tomato and cook until it breaks down.
Stir the fried mixture into the lentils, add salt and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Garnish with coriander and serve with red rice.

title: Egg Datshi
instructions: Heat the oil and soften the sliced onion and chilies for 3 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato and cook until soft.
Pour in the lightly beaten eggs and stir gently until just set.
Fold in the cheese, cover and let it melt for 2 minutes.
Serve with rice or Tingmo.
